explanation: Eating quietly is a core part of British table manners, and slurping noodles or soup is generally seen as impolite and a bit uncouth. This isn't specific to noodles - Western table manners broadly discourage making noise with food or cutlery - so the norm applies in both casual and formal UK dining settings.
local_tip: Twirl noodles discreetly around your fork or spoon and eat quietly, as you would with any other dish in the UK.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles like ramen or soba is a sign of enjoyment and is not considered rude.
Slurping noodles is common and seen as showing appreciation, though it may be toned down in very formal settings.
Slurping pasta is considered poor manners; pasta is twirled onto a fork and eaten quietly.
